claims.text: The primary source states that \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]

**Conditional presentation-and-Pieri certificate.** Assume the integral interval presentation for \(p=c=1\), namely \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\), \(d=ij\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and \[ M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{\substack{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\\|\mu|=d+k}}\mathbb Zs_\mu \quad(0\le k\le b), \] with complete \(h_1\)-row set \[ \{h_1s_\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1},\ |\lambda|=d+k-1\}. \] Then, for \(1\le k\le b\), putting \[ P_{x,y}:=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{\,j-x},y)} \quad(y=0\text{ omitted}), \] one has \[ M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=0}^{k}\mathbb ZP_{x,k-x}, \] and its complete \(h_1\)-row set is precisely \[ h_1P_{x,k-1-x}=P_{x+1,k-1-x}+P_{x,k-x} \qquad(0\le x\le k-1). \] Thus the row lattice is \[ L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}),\qquad C_x=P_{x,k-x}. \] Deleting \(C_0\), respectively \(C_k\), gives lower-, respectively upper-, unitriangular \(k\times k\) matrices, both of determinant \(1\). For \(k=0\), \(M_d=\mathbb Zs_{i^j}\), the row set is empty, and the empty complementary determinant is \(1\).
